summary: Clallam County, WA pole platform lookout built 1933 on Olympic National Forest land; 1935 fire date disputed; reported collapsed in 2025.

facts.design: Pole platform tower of standing snags and poles
facts.status_note: Collapsed; TrailChick gives April 2025 as the date reported, and firelookout.com says it collapsed over the winter of 2024/2025

staffing.status: A fire guard from Slab Camp Creek manned it when fire danger was high (visitor page; no dates given)

access.note: On Olympic National Forest land with a hiking route to the site; no closure is described in the sources read

visit.trail_note: Walk the hiker trail from a gravel-road trailhead; directions begin at the west end of Sequim on Highway 101. Sources differ on length (1.1 miles per a visitor page; TrailChick gives a usual distance of 2.2). A visitor page warns that climbing will bring down pieces.

events.note: Constructed 1933 per the register; firelookout.com says it was a pole platform tower built in 1933; a visitor page describes standing snags and poles
TrailChick says the Maynard Peak fire burned over the area and the lookout's two main posts in 1935. A visitor page says the fire was in 'the early part of the century'. The year is disputed.
Panorama photos taken August 21, 1935 (Washington Lookouts page); TrailChick credits the 1935 panoramas to the USFS
Collapsed. TrailChick reports April 2025; firelookout.com says over the winter of 2024/2025.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: TrailChick dates the Maynard Peak fire to 1935; the visitor page says 'the early part of the century' and mentions the 1935 photo survey. The story reports both and says the sources do not agree on the year.
firelookout.com says it collapsed over the winter of 2024/2025; TrailChick says it was reported collapsed in April 2025. Both are kept.
A visitor page gives 1.1 miles; TrailChick gives a usual distance of 2.2 without a clear unit or direction. The story reports both.
The register gives 3,458 ft (1,054 m), firelookout.com and a visitor page give about 3,450 ft, and TrailChick gives 3,464 ft. The brief's 1,054 m is kept.

notes_for_editor: Brief said access unknown; the sources describe a public hiking route on Olympic National Forest land, so access is recorded as public. Unread lead: a Summer 2025 Olympic National Forest-related article (https://firelookout.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/Birdseye-view_Fire-Lookouts-Then-and-Now.pdf) appeared only as a search snippet, and it reportedly names Ned Hill among two 'public lookouts'. That conflicts with the 'gone' status and should be read before publishing. A Facebook post saying what 'remains' of the lookout was also seen only as a snippet and is not cited. What is left at the site now is not described in any source read. The brief's 'platform' kind is kept as 'pole platform'.
